Lessons.Title: Fitting Linear Models to Data
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning aims: draw and interpret scatterplots, identify a reasonable line of best fit, distinguish linear versus nonlinear patterns and predict from a linear model.
A least-squares model y=mx+b minimizes the sum of squared vertical residuals; an approximate hand-drawn line is different from a mathematical regression computation.
Pearson's r ranges from −1 through +1, with sign indicating association direction and magnitude reflecting linear association strength. Correlation does not establish causation.
Interpolation predicts at an x within the observed window. Extrapolation predicts outside it and requires an explicit caution about model reliability.
Always state the data units, observed x-range, the fitted slope/intercept and whether the graph has a curved residual pattern.
Independent Edulytics Cool-down: Given paired data (0,2),(1,4),(2,6),(3,8): (a) fit an exact linear rule, (b) identify r, (c) predict at x=2.5 and x=7 and classify each prediction.
Independent Try It 1 — Predict within observed x-range. A fitted line for x∈[0,4] is y=2.2x+3. Evaluate at x=2 and classify prediction.
Independent Try It 2 — Extrapolate line with model caution. For y=2.2x+3 fitted on x=0..4, predict at x=6; identify whether extrapolation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Scatterplot
KeyConcepts.Definition: Each paired numerical observation (x,y) is plotted as one point.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not connect observations unless their order and process justify it.

KeyConcepts.Title: Visual best-fit line
KeyConcepts.Definition: A line that follows the pattern of a scatterplot; not necessarily a perfect match.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Predict only when the relationship appears sufficiently straight.

KeyConcepts.Title: Least-squares regression
KeyConcepts.Definition: Choose coefficients m,b minimizing the sum of squared vertical residuals.

KeyConcepts.Title: Residual
KeyConcepts.Rule: A pattern in residuals can indicate an inadequate linear model.

KeyConcepts.Title: Pearson correlation
KeyConcepts.Definition: r measures direction and strength of linear association, between −1 and 1.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Large |r| means close to line, not proof of causation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Interpolation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Estimating within the span of observed independent inputs.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Predictions can still be wrong even inside observed span.

KeyConcepts.Title: Extrapolation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Estimating beyond original independent input range.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Explicitly flag changing conditions and weaker reliability.

KeyConcepts.Title: Nonlinear relations
KeyConcepts.Definition: Curved scatter patterns are not well described by one affine rule.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Inspect scatter and residual shape before using regression.
KeyConcepts.Example: x² data curve instead of straight line.

KeyConcepts.Title: Correlation sign
KeyConcepts.Definition: Positive correlation indicates y grows on average with x; negative falls.
KeyConcepts.Rule: r near 0 means weak linear relation, not necessarily no relation.

Visuals.Title: First-party five-observation scatter data
Visuals.Description: A near-linear dataset rather than an identical publisher chart.

Visuals.Title: Interpolation and extrapolation
Visuals.Description: The source dataset has measured inputs from zero through four.

SummaryPoints: Determine whether linear fit is sensible.
Least squares minimizes vertical squared residuals.
Correlation sign and magnitude describe linear association, not causation.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming an r near one means the slope must be one.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Correlation is unitless; slope is output/input units.
A third variable or coincidence can create association.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating long-distance extrapolation as confirmed fact.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The observed relationship may break outside the sampled range.
CommonMistakes.Correction: State data window, forecast assumptions and caution.
